related_not_profiled.note: 8F56 quartz GMT perpetual-calendar titanium Alpinists from 2003 (SSASS: 500-pc blue charity edition) per Fratello; predate SARB era, end date not verified.

6R15 Seiko Mechanical models that are NOT Alpinists (SARB011: 10 bar see-through back; SARB065: Cocktail Time-style elegant model; SARB033/035: standard models). SARB001/003/005 appear only inside an HTML comment on the 2007 Alpinist page.

history_facts.text: Seiko states its first Alpinist was introduced in 1959 'to meet the needs of mountain climbers and recreational field sports enthusiasts' and was 'the first Seiko watch ever produced with sports in mind'.
The Alpinist name returned in 1995 with the SCVF005 (black), SCVF007 (cream) and SCVF009 (green) on the 4S15 calibre, introducing the 4 o'clock compass crown and cathedral hands.
Seiko Japan's Mechanical lineup listed SARB013, SARB015 and SARB017 under 'アルピニスト' and marked all three 'NEW' in a March 2007 capture.

Seiko Japan called the line a 'trekking model' (トレッキングモデル「アルピニスト」) with a simple compass, screw-lock crown and 20-bar water resistance, and described the Alpinist symbol on the caseback as based on a mountain range.

Seiko's compass method: set N on the ring to 12 o'clock, hold the watch level, point the 24-hour hand (or hour hand) at the sun, and read the bearing. Seiko notes it works only in the Northern Hemisphere and may not work seasonally south of the Tropic of Cancer.
In 2009 Seiko added SARB059 and SARB061 plus the 500-piece SARB063 made with nature photographer Takeshi Mizukoshi to the Alpinist group. Their dials print nine ground-to-air emergency signal codes.
Seiko Japan's Alpinist group shrank over time: SARB059/061/015/017 in June 2010, SARB059/017 in November 2011 and June 2013, and SARB017 alone by June 2015.
SARB017's discontinuation was reported in February–March 2018, citing JDM dealer Seiya Japan, alongside SARB033/SARB035.
Seiko USA released the blue SPB089 in 2019, limited to 1,959 pieces at US$600, with a serial number on the caseback.
In 2020 the line moved into Prospex as SPB117/119/121 (plus SPB123) with the 6R35 (70 h), a display caseback and the Prospex 'X' on the dial instead of an Alpinist script.
